title: Feature probe can dereference past argv when run without arguments
reasoning: main reads argv[argc-1] and passes it to _mm512_loadu_si512. If the binary is executed with argc == 0 in a nonstandard process launch, this indexes before argv. More commonly with argc == 1 it reads from argv[0], which is a short NUL-terminated string and the 64-byte unaligned vector load can read beyond the argument string object. As a compile/run feature check this may usually be invoked by build tooling rather than end users, so severity is low, but the top-level CLI entrypoint is not robust to its declared user-input/process-exec boundary.
recommendation: Avoid loading from argv storage. Use a local aligned or unaligned 64-byte buffer initialized in the function, or guard argc and input length before loading from argv.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included for this feature probe or for direct execution behavior.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a build/probe test that compiles and executes cpu_avx512_icl with no extra CLI arguments under the expected probe harness and verifies it exits without invalid memory access on supported hardware or an emulator environment.
minimumFixScope: Change main to load from a local 64-byte buffer instead of argv, preserving the intrinsic calls used to validate compiler support.

history.note: Excluded vendored frontend/python-runtime dependency probe from WindieOS-owned review scope
